text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for people who did not write it. One key idea is using clear naming conventions, so variables have meaningful names like "totalPrice" instead of "x". Another key idea is keeping functions small and focused on one task, which makes them easier to test and reuse. Finally, clean code improves maintainability, meaning it is simpler to fix bugs or add new features later. When you write code that others can read easily, your whole team works faster and makes fewer mistakes.
